newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks down by lunch, investors sidelined.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks down by lunch, investors sidelined.

text.p: Thai stocks fell by the lunch break on Wednesday in slow trade as short-term concerns kept investors away from the troubled market, traders said.
The SET index went into lunch down 5.04 points, or 0.88 percent, at 564.80. The SET 50 fell 0.39 points to 40.89 in subdued trade worth a meagre 668 million baht.

A possible drop in first-quarter profit figures expected from conglomerate Siam Cement Plc later, an afternoon briefing on troubled Finance One's prospects and the release of economic data on Thursday had investors sidelined pending developments, traders said.
"I think people are waiting on the result of SCC (Siam Cement) later and are worried that earnings may be lower then expectations," said a trader at the Multi Credit Corporation.
"People also want to hear about Finance One from the meeting this afternoon," she said. The firm's suspended shares resume trading on Friday and are expected to drag the market down.
A release of economic data due from the central bank on Thursday also has investors biding time, analysts said.
Bangkok Bank Plc was unchanged at 149, while Thai Farmers Bank Plc lost 1.25 baht to 99.50. Land and House dipped 17.50 to 28 as its shares went ex-rights.
